text.p: Year to March 31 1997.
(Figures in millions of French francs unless stated)
Net attributable (cons.) profit 394 vs loss 2,264

The consolidated result takes accounts of subsidiaries such as Servair, Air Charter, and Jet Tour but not the short and medium haul airline formerly called Air Inter, which is due to merge with its parent and due to publish its own results separately.
Restated Accounts of Air France (excluding subsidiaries):
Turnover 42,706 vs 39,442
Gross profit 4,448 vs 4,051
Operating profit 1,171 vs 413
Pre-tax profit 129 vs loss 968
Restated net result profit 211 vs loss 2,873
NOTE: The 1995-96 net profit figure includes restructuring charges.
The company said in a statement the increase in turnover was due to sustained growth in passenger and baggage revenue, which rose 10.5 percent or 2.7 billion francs.
"In an economically unfavourable context, Air France cargo operations showed a 5.5 percent increase in traffic for a 4.4 percent increase in capacity," it said.
"External supplies were adversely affected by the significant rise in fuel costs over this period. The price increase alone accounted for 900 million francs," it said.
It said labour costs remained stable and that the average weighted staff count dropped to 36,173 from 36,484.
Air France net financial debt, including quasi-equity, dropped 5.2 billion francs to a little under 14 billion francs at March 31, 1997, it said.

"This was primarily because of cash flow -- three billion francs -- covered almost all the year's investments of 3.1 billion francs, which included the first instalments for the renewal of the fleet at the end of the year," it said.
The results were issued after a board meeting on Thursday.
Consolidated turnover 46,402 vs 43,226
Operating profit 1,138 vs 420
Pre-tax profit 39 vs loss 858
NOTE: The above figures are those supplied in a statement under the heading "Consolidated Results of Air France 1996-97".
